question: Should OpenClaw core support native per-task model hints in HEARTBEAT.md, or should heartbeat model routing remain per-turn and plugin-owned until a broader scheduled-routing design lands?
rationale: Source inspection proves the capability is missing, but adding it changes public HEARTBEAT.md syntax, model precedence, task execution grouping, and session-state semantics; automation should not choose that API shape.

options.title: Add native task hints
options.body: Define model/provider fields for HEARTBEAT.md tasks, group or split due tasks by effective model, and add tests/docs for precedence, timestamps, and session restoration.

options.title: Keep whole-turn routing
options.body: Document that heartbeat.model and before_model_resolve route an entire heartbeat tick, accepting that exact per-task escalation is not supported in core.

options.title: Fold into scheduled routing
options.body: Defer this to the broader scheduled model override track so cron and heartbeat use one shared model-routing contract instead of a HEARTBEAT-specific syntax.

recommendation.title: Add native task hints
recommendation.body: Define model/provider fields for HEARTBEAT.md tasks, group or split due tasks by effective model, and add tests/docs for precedence, timestamps, and session restoration.

likelyOwner.reason: The current heartbeat parser/runner history and active model/config surface work make this the best available owner for choosing a safe implementation boundary.
